family.meaning: name is the family's name, compared as written. data is the kind of storage pool its columns are kept in. compression and cache_mode are the family's settings. keep_in_memory is a setting only a table profile gives, which no statement writes. columns are the columns the family holds; the default family lists none. A setting left out is not stated.

ptah.run/ydb/column-families.constraint: Family names are unique, and a column is in one family at most. A setting the value leaves out keeps what the table holds, and so does a family the table holds and the value leaves out. A column the value places in no family sits in the default family. The value's absence under complete source coverage requests no family of the table's columns.
Every family the table holds, with each setting as YDB reports it, YDB's own values included. A table whose families hold a setting the read does not model is recorded in coverage instead.

canonicalization: Families are written sorted by name, and each family's columns sorted. Strings must be valid UTF-8 and are kept verbatim; compression and cache_mode are in lower case.
